reviewed_contracts: 00 binds exactly retained run IDs 23758/23767/23776, recorded start/end times, one current job, fixed command SHA and the recorded enqueue definition; missing, changed, over-cap or unknown input is STOP.
00 returns only fixed failure classifications, bounded full-message hashes, byte lengths and safe metadata. SQLSTATE mappings are always reference codes, never claimed original SQLSTATE observations.
01 returns safe catalog shapes and fingerprints; raw setconfig/proconfig/proargdefaults or function definitions are not returned. All 14 known optional relation absences are checked explicitly.
01 and 10/20 explicitly verify the six queue columns and the sole pure legacy nextval ID default. The legacy default and its nontransactional counter consumption remain part of the stated contract.
10/20 stop on the intentionally missing independent native_transport_sha256 before temporary objects or installation DDL; the fixed V2 catalog digest anchors the existing protected chain.
10/20 acquire the queue barrier and fixed ledger/history locks before a fresh READ COMMITTED high-water read; the 1024-number reserve does not replace those barriers or the exact inventory.
The owned LOGGED sequence and narrow SECURITY DEFINER trigger helper use the fixed queue/operation/name/context and fully qualified nextval/regclass target; new allocator ACLs are checked owner-only.
The source publisher receives an exact early qualification/original-byte barrier. Its negative call must be IS DISTINCT FROM 0 to fail; no positive qualification or renewal is inferred.
The additive Production v3-to-v4 guard successor preserves prior baseline rows and constrains existing catalog deltas to the five reviewed function definitions and explicitly new objects.

10 checks real queue INSERT RETURNING values with INTO STRICT and null-safe equality, owned-sequence RESTART rollback, helper dependency restoration, guard refusal and baseline immutability; these are prepared runtime assertions, not executed proofs.
20 consumes no queue probe IDs and distinguishes a pre-COMMIT result row from actual successful COMMIT completion and the later independent readback.

30/40 require the independent actual committed-successor pin, change only the pinned helper, retain existing queued work and counters, and distinguish synchronous helper/catalog refusal from periodic public audit/alarm behavior.
